title: Henriette de Clèves and Renato Birago to the duke of Nevers, Lyon, September 1574, BnF fr. 3315 ff. 15-16, 21

steps.what: Mapped manuscript folios to Gallica openings and fetched full-resolution images of ff. 15 and 21 and the neighbouring keys.
Found and transcribed the complete clear Italian fair copy beneath Birago's cipher flap at f. 21.
Identified the small writing between the cipher lines of f. 15 as a contemporary word-by-word decipherment, not random pen trials.
Fetched Nevers no. 2 of 1584 from BnF fr. 3995 f. 16 and confirmed that it is only a sibling key, not the exact target alphabet.
Checked a superficially similar Henri III appeal printed by Lavisse and rejected it as a crib because it predates this letter and has a different sender.
Read the opening on f. 15 and the clear ending on f. 16r; continuous transcription of the cipher leaves remained blocked by the overwritten minute hand.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): decryptions f15_reading.md (opening, address and clear ending only) and f21_transcription.md (the clear fair copy); no sign-level transcription of either cipher exists in the folder

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): f21_transcription.md reads as continuous Italian (reviewed A); f15_reading.md gives only the opening of the gloss, the address and the clear closing, so f. 15 is relabelled decoded, not read. fraction_read 0.4 -> about 0.3 (estimated).

outcome.method_basis: f. 21 was read from the complete contemporary clear copy under Birago's cipher flap, and the opening of f. 15 from its contemporary interlinear decipherment and the clear ending on f. 16r; no key was applied (the 1584 Nevers no. 2 alphabet in fr. 3995 is close but not the key).
outcome.fraction_read_source: Reading audit 22 Oct 2026: of the cipher, only Birago's f. 21 reads (its clear fair copy, 271 words); the two dense cipher pages of f. 15 are decoded, not read (the opening of the gloss only), and the f. 16r closing is clear text, not cipher. Rough page-weighted estimate, not a token count. Withdrawn: 0.4, which counted the f. 15 opening and the clear closing.
outcome.notes: The target is not wholly undecrypted: both leaves preserve their own reading aids. f. 21 is complete; f. 15 remains palaeographically incomplete.

gaps.detail: Minute interlinear French is crossed by larger cipher signs and locally faded; enlarged crop pass recovered anchors but not a defensible continuous text.
1584 Nevers no. 2 is similar but differs. Exact table could be rebuilt by glyph-level alignment of the f. 21 cipher slip with its interlinear Italian gloss.
Fair copy appears to read 'per saluato suo'; perhaps a personal name or abbreviation.

credits.note: clear copy under the cipher flap (f. 21) and interlinear decipherment of f. 15

texts.label: Henriette de Clèves to the duke of Nevers, Lyon, 16 Sept [1574], ff. 15-16
texts.note: f15_reading.md gives only the opening of the interlinear decipherment, the address and the clear closing on f. 16r (not cipher); the two enciphered pages themselves are not transcribed, so their text is not read
texts.summary: The duchess of Nevers writes to her husband; a contemporary reader wrote a word-by-word French decipherment between the cipher lines. Only the opening, the address and the clear ending on f. 16r are edited: it is midnight, her eyes hurt from weeping, and seeing how they are treated she would rather be in paradise. No transcription of the cipher signs or continuous transcription of the interlinear gloss exists (the gloss is too crowded to transcribe defensibly).

texts.label: Renato Birago to the duke of Nevers, Lyon, 28 Sept 1574, f. 21

reading_review.note: f21_transcription.md: the contemporary clear fair copy under the cipher flap, transcribed as continuous Italian; every sentence reads, one doubtful word (saluato suo).

texts.summary: Birago had expected Nevers in Lyon for St Michael's day; the bearer's business comes at the worst moment, as the affairs of the kingdom make anything else more urgent; Birago will speak of Piedmont by mouth; Their Majesties are well disposed to give Nevers a government and whatever else he deserves. The decryption is the clear fair copy on the same recto; the cipher flap itself was not transcribed sign by sign.

prior.where: The manuscript itself preserves a contemporary interlinear decipherment on f. 15, a clear ending on f. 16r, and a complete clear copy under the cipher flap on f. 21; Tomokiyo described the system but published no reading.

human: The human selected the target and requested a solve/read followed by a write-up. No target-specific transcription or cryptanalytic intervention.
